gen-gf-offside-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Curves that refuse to close give Offside its restless, widely spaced look, drawn with no swelling anywhere. Noto Sans Nushu sits beneath with a towering x-height and terminals held away from the stroke, so long paragraphs feel open and tall.
gen-gf-offside-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Offside runs wide and level, every glyph drawn with one flat line weight and curves left unclosed. Noto Sans Ogham takes over below, its tall bodies making the lowercase look bold, and that heft against the thin heading is the pair's strongest single quality.
gen-gf-offside-gf-noto-sans-ol-chiki: Wide-set, flat-lined lettering up top, then a body of solid word blocks: that is the whole look here. Offside is best at making a statement with unvarying strokes; Noto Sans Ol Chiki simply keeps text steady.
gen-gf-offside-gf-noto-sans-old-hungaria: Commanding, wire-thin and widely spaced, Offside takes the lead. Its open curves announce things, while Noto Sans Old Hungarian, a plain sans with roomy a, e and s shapes, stays legible down at tiny sizes.
gen-gf-offside-gf-noto-sans-old-italic: Offside traces every letter with a line of constant weight, spaced wide and left deliberately unclosed in its curves. Noto Sans Old Italic handles the reading, with little gap between lowercase and capitals and curve endings kept apart, while the heading does the announcing.
gen-gf-offside-gf-noto-sans-old-north-ar: Noto Sans Old North Arabian packs a dense, tall lowercase band with terminals flaring outward like tongs. Make the heading small, though, and Offside's wire-like monoline skeleton loses its wide-set authority, while the body keeps its weight at any size.
gen-gf-offside-gf-noto-sans-old-permic: Noto Sans Old Permic is rounded and open to the side, with lowercase almost as tall as its capitals. Give that plain sans a little extra size and its forms breathe, while Offside's one-pen-tip lines stay out of the way.
gen-gf-offside-gf-noto-sans-old-persian: A single pen-tip simplicity runs through every Offside glyph, spaced wide with curves left open. Noto Sans Old Persian, a plain sans with lofty lowercase, reads freely.
gen-gf-offside-gf-noto-sans-old-sogdian: Noto Sans Old Sogdian has a tall x-height nearly reaching cap height, and its wide-mouthed letters stay crisp when shrunk. Yet Offside, with no shading from thick to thin, keeps the heading quiet, so a long read feels steady and clear.
gen-gf-offside-gf-noto-sans-old-turkic: Wire-cut strokes, wide spacing and curves that never quite close make Offside look like a signal fire. Noto Sans Old Turkic grounds it with chunky, open lowercase.
